findings.summary: Hand-traced mutation not caught by any test in the file, nor by any other test in the suite (grep confirms LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest.java is the only caller of firstInheritableAncestor). Mutating `boolean atOrigin = true;` to `boolean atOrigin = false;` in `firstInheritableAncestor` only changes behaviour on the FIRST loop check (chainEpoch == prevEpoch), and only when `firstEntry(prevEpoch)` is null -- neverOpened's Seal-branch never consults atOrigin, and the loop body unconditionally sets atOrigin=false after the first iteration, so every subsequent check is identical under both the true and false initial value. All three fixtures in this file deliberately give the walk's origin (prevEpoch, i.e. epoch-1) a Seal-shaped or Continue-shaped slot 0 -- test 1 and test 3 both state in-comment that this is 'for the same atOrigin reason ... an empty chain AT THE ORIGIN is neverOpened's own disclosed (M4.23) gap, not this walk's to close' -- so none of the fixtures ever exercises the null-at-origin branch this variable's initial value controls.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that flips `atOrigin`'s initial value (or a future refactor that accidentally passes `false` on the first neverOpened call) would silently change firstInheritableAncestor's behaviour for a wholly-empty immediate predecessor -- from 'stop, report prevEpoch as inheritable and inherit nothing' (today's documented M4.23-scoped behaviour, matching inherited()'s existing origin caveat) to 'walk past it and keep searching'. Neither is exercised by any test, so the change would be invisible.

notes: Task: verify the two new test methods in LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest.java close the two gaps named in the round-1 finding (the seal-before-open ordering claim, and the firstInheritableAncestor `chainEpoch >= 1` loop boundary).

ORDER-SWAP MUTATION (LocalSequencer.start, seal-then-open): hand-traced against test 2 (aRedrivenSealsExtraDeltaReachesTheSuccessorProvingOrderIsLoadBearing) using the fixture's actual sequence numbers. Correct order: predecessor.recoverChainEnd() snapshots nextSequence=2 (slots 0,1 exist), predecessor.seal(2, budget) then contends for slot 2 with StealFirstPutStore's injected in-flight delta (RunCommit(count=2, firstOffset=3) -> lastOffset=4), loses, folds it, redrives to slot 3, returns Seal(sequence=3). log.open(1, 3) crosses via ChainReplay.inherited(...,1,3), which lists epoch 1 up to sequence<=3 and now includes the in-flight delta at slot 2 (already landed by the time open() runs) -- offsets fold to next=5 for the stream (max(3, 4+1)). The successor's next commit's firstOffset is therefore 5, matching the assertion. Under a swapped order (open reads BEFORE the contested seal write happens -- concretely, sourcing prevSeq from recoverChainEnd()'s pre-redrive nextSequence=2 and calling open before seal), crossFrom(1,2) would list epoch 1 at that earlier moment, before the thief write to slot 2 has occurred (StealFirstPutStore only writes it on the FIRST putIfAbsent to that key, which happens inside seal()), so it would see only slots 0-1 and compute next=3 -- the successor would then hand out firstOffset 3, colliding with the in-flight delta's own 3-4. The test's isEqualTo(5) assertion would fail under this mutation: caught.

Confirmed the claimed ASYMMETRY by tracing test 1 (aTakeoverSealsTheAncestorItINHERITSFromNotBlindlyEpochMinusOne) against the same order-swap: its fixture is fully written before start() ever runs and uses no StealFirstPutStore, so recoverChainEnd()'s pre-seal snapshot (nextSequence=2) and seal()'s actual write (uncontested, lands at slot 2, sequence=2) agree -- prevSeq is 2 either order, log.open(1,2) reads the identical store state either order, and the zombie is still fenced once seal() eventually runs (order of the two calls doesn't change whether seal() itself succeeds). Test 1 would pass unchanged under the order-swap: exactly the asymmetry the new test's own comment claims, hand-confirmed rather than taken on faith.

LOOP BOUNDARY MUTATION (`chainEpoch >= 1` -> `chainEpoch > 1` in firstInheritableAncestor): hand-traced test 3 (aWalkWithNoGenuineAncestorAnywhereStopsAtZeroRatherThanSealingAnUnopenedEpoch). Correct walk from prevEpoch=4 (Seal shape) through empty epochs 3,2,1 (all neverOpened=true) reaches chainEpoch=0, where `0 >= 1` is false, loop exits, returns 0. Under `> 1`, the walk stops one iteration early: at chainEpoch=1, `1 > 1` is false, so epoch 1 (genuinely empty, never opened) is never inspected and is wrongly returned as the inheritable ancestor. LocalSequencer.start would then seal epoch 1 (a chain that was never opened) and the CONTINUE would name prevEpoch=1 instead of 0 -- both the `opening.prevEpoch()).isZero()` assertion and the `epoch 1 ... must not seal it` loop assertion (e=1..3) fail under this mutation: caught.

Confirmed the mutation is NOT caught by test 1 or test 2: in both fixtures the real ancestor is exactly at epoch 1, so the walk's guard condition is never the thing that decides whether epoch 1 gets checked -- in test 1, chainEpoch reaches 1 after two decrements from 3, and `1 >= 1` and `1 > 1` diverge (true vs false) only at that check, but firstEntry(1) is a genuine Continue so the loop would have stopped there anyway under the correct guard; the `> 1` mutant returns 1 without checking it, which happens to be the SAME answer. In test 2 the walk never enters its loop body at all (prevEpoch=1 already fails neverOpened on the very first check under either guard, since epoch 1 is genuinely opened there too). Both converge on the same output as the correct implementation by coincidence of where the real ancestor sits -- exactly the surviving-mutation shape the round-1 finding named, and exactly why test 3 had to be built with NO genuine ancestor anywhere in the walk.

Checked a related boundary NOT part of the round-1 finding: `if (prevEpoch >= 1)` in LocalSequencer.start (unchanged, pre-existing code) mutated to `>= 0`. Test 3 produces prevEpoch=0 via the new walk-to-zero path, but a `>=0` mutant would seal the RESERVED epoch-0 chain there without any assertion in test 3 noticing (it only checks epochs 1-3 are untouched, never epoch 0, and the CONTINUE written is identical either way since prevSeq also lands on 0). This gap is closed by a PRE-EXISTING, unmodified test elsewhere in the suite -- LocalSequencerTest#theFirstLeaderDoesNotTouchTheReservedUnleasedChain, whose own comment states it was 'FOUND BY MUTATION: prevEpoch >= 1 -> >= 0 killed nothing'. That test seeds epoch 0 with real content first, so any accidental seal of epoch 0 grows its object count and fails the `isEqualTo(before)` assertion regardless of which caller path (direct epoch-1 vs the new walk) produced prevEpoch=0. Not a gap in the suite as a whole; noting it because the task asked to look for any other mutation the two new tests specifically would not catch, and this one would slip past all three tests in the new file even though the full suite catches it elsewhere.

Verified `.harness/tdd/red.json` (not gitignored from this reasoning, read directly): all three test methods in LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest.java have red records -- aRedrivenSealsExtraDeltaReachesTheSuccessorProvingOrderIsLoadBearing, aTakeoverSealsTheAncestorItINHERITSFromNotBlindlyEpochMinusOne, and aWalkWithNoGenuineAncestorAnywhereStopsAtZeroRatherThanSealingAnUnopenedEpoch, each with a distinct timestamp (~22:26 UTC, roughly 8 minutes before this review) and a sha256 tied to LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest.java. Consistent with three separate red observations rather than one copied record.

Checked LocalSequencerFailoverTest's updated numbers for internal consistency (not independently recomputed from an empty baseline, since no gradle run was available in this environment): every scenario in the aTakeoverReadsEveryEntryOfEveryANCESTORAndTHATISAREGRESSION test moved by exactly +1 on gets() and +2 on total() relative to the round-1-reviewed values (17->18, 45->46 gets; 26->28, 54->56, 18->20, 45->47 totals), uniformly across all six assertions regardless of entry count or term count. This matches the single fixed cost the diff actually adds: firstEntry() -> one stat (always) plus one get (when the slot is occupied), issued exactly once per takeover in every one of these fixtures because none of them burn epochs, so the immediate predecessor's slot 0 is always a genuine CONTINUE and the walk never iterates past the first check. No drift, no per-entry or per-term scaling introduced.

Verdict: pass. Both mutations named in the round-1 finding are hand-confirmed caught by the intended new test and hand-confirmed NOT caught by the other two -- the asymmetry claimed for test 1 vs test 2 on the ordering mutation is real, and the round-1 boundary gap is closed by test 3 alone, not incidentally by test 1 or test 2. One minor, non-blocking finding (F1) on an untested initialization value that only matters for a case explicitly and consistently scoped out of this task (M4.23) in every fixture's own comments.
